description:
A humanitarian convoy to evacuate as many as 750 civilians has left the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in Ukraine.

Oleshky has been under Russian control since the first days of the invasion in February 2022. Thousands have been trapped there, and many have reported eating garden weeds to survive.

Evacuated residents were given the choice to leave Russian-occupied territory and return to Ukraine through Belarus, or to resettle in Russia. The operation is also bringing food, medicine, fuel and other supplies.

Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets says joint aid will be delivered to all residents who remain in Oleshky, and help given to those leaving for Ukraine or Russia. Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova thanked her counterpart for ensuring the ceasefire was maintained.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says this is an isolated humanitarian arrangement coordinated with the US, and not a sign of any breakthrough in peace negotiations.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Florida voters will decide on Amendment 3 in the midterms, a state constitutional amendment that would raise the property tax exemption. Conservationists fear it could put Everglades restoration projects at risk and could also lead to the loss of conservation lands.

Currently, the first $50,000 of non-school property tax on a primary home is exempt. If the amendment passes, that would rise to $150,000 next year, then to $250,000 in 2028, and then increase with inflation.

Estimates suggest it could save a typical homeowner about $2,000 a year, but could also blow an almost $12 billion hole in annual local government revenue. Some police officers, sheriffs, firefighters and librarians have sounded the alarm that it could affect their departments. Even some conservative voices have warned it could shift the tax burden onto other sectors.

The amendment needs 60% of the votes to pass on November 3.

Al Jazeera’s John Holman reports from Florida.

Subscribe to our channel: http://bit.ly/
title: Florida votes on property tax cut in midterms as Everglades backers warn of funding risk
